_comment: Structure WS2 — DERIVED. No printed answer key; every answer derived from first principles. REVIEW-flagged items need a human spot-check (source typos or duplicate options).

1.reason: Isotopes: same chemical properties (1, true) and atoms of the same element (4, true). Same atomic masses (2) is false — isotopes have different masses; different atomic numbers (3) is false — isotopes have the same Z. So (a) and (d).

2.reason: REVIEW: Al has Z=13, configuration 2,8,3. Options (b) and (c) are both printed identically as 2,8,3 (source duplicate); chose (b) as the first correct occurrence.

4.reason: Statement 1 (isobars have different chemical properties) is true. Statement 2 (sum of protons and neutrons always different) is false — isobars have the SAME mass number, i.e. the same p+n sum. So S1 true, S2 false.

5.reason: 15 electrons in a neutral atom means Z=15; mass number = protons + neutrons = 15 + 16 = 31, giving 31/15 X.

6.reason: Configuration 2,8,4 has 4 valence electrons — characteristic of a metalloid (e.g. silicon).

7.reason: Isoelectronic species have equal electrons. Na+ (10), O2- (10) and Ne (10) all have 10 electrons. (a) has O with 8; (c) has Al with 13; (d) Cl-/Ar/Ca have 18/18/20.

8.reason: charge/mass: deuterium = 1/2, alpha-particle = 2/4 = 1/2 — identical. Proton = 1/1; electron carries no comparable match here.

9.reason: Mass 27, neutrons 14 -> protons = 13. The ion has charge 3+, so electrons = 13 - 3 = 10.

10.reason: Isotopes have the same atomic number, different mass number. 226/88 A and 228/88 C both have Z=88 with masses 226 and 228.

11.reason: The first model of the atom (plum-pudding) was given by J.J. Thomson.

12.reason: In Rutherford's experiment most particles pass undeflected, a few deflect through small angles, and a very few through large angles — row III.

14.reason: Ordinary hydrogen (protium) has 1 proton and 1 electron but no neutron.

15.reason: A (9p,9e) is fluorine, valency 1, forms F-. B (12p,12e) is magnesium, valency 2, forms Mg2+. The compound is MgF2 = B A2.

16.reason: Deuterium, Tritium and Protium are isotopes of hydrogen (same Z=1). Argon (~40) and Calcium (~40) are isobars (same mass, different Z).

17.reason: Rutherford's alpha-scattering experiment led to the discovery of the atomic nucleus.

18.reason: Cathode rays are streams of electrons — they carry both charge and mass.

19.reason: Anode (positive) rays have the highest e/m for the lightest gas, since e/m is largest when mass is smallest — hydrogen.

20.reason: REVIEW: source table's second row is mislabelled 'Protons' (8,10) but is clearly Neutrons. X (8p,8n) and Y (8p,10n) have the same protons -> isotopes -> same chemical, different physical properties; only (c) is correct. (a) different chemical is false; (b) isobars is false; (d) all-correct false.

21.reason: More electrons than protons means net negative charge -> anion.

22.reason: Dalton's theory explained conservation of mass (i), constant composition (ii) and multiple proportions (iv). It did NOT explain radioactivity (iii).

23.reason: Isotopes (same Z) have the same chemical properties; isobars (same mass, different Z) have different chemical properties.

24.reason: Isobars have the same mass number, different atomic number: Ar-40 (Z=18) and Ca-40 (Z=20).

25.reason: Carbon isotopes all have 6 protons: C-12 = 6p+6n, C-13 = 6p+7n, C-14 = 6p+8n.

26.reason: Rutherford's conclusions: small dense nucleus (a, d) and Coulombic repulsion (c). 'Positively charged particles of the atom move with very high velocity' (b) is NOT a conclusion — the fast-moving particles were the alpha projectiles, not the atom's contents.

27.reason: Z: U19,V53,W17,X35,Y18 -> ascending W<Y<U<X<V, so statement 1 (U<W<X<V<Y) is INCORRECT. Statement 2 mass order W<U<Y<X<V is correct. Statement 3 (orders differ) is correct. Statement 4 (protons=neutrons in all) is INCORRECT (e.g. U has 19p,20n). Incorrect = i and iv.

28.reason: Most alpha-particles pass straight through because the nucleus occupies a very small fraction of the atom's volume — the atom is mostly empty space.

29.reason: Bohr postulated that electrons in fixed orbits do NOT radiate energy. Statement (b) — electrons radiate energy during revolution — is the classical (Rutherford) idea Bohr explicitly rejected.

30.reason: 3 valence electrons in the 3rd (outermost) shell means configuration 2,8,3 -> Z=13 = aluminium. (Boron 2,3 is in the 2nd shell.)

31.reason: Chadwick's neutron-discovery reaction: Be-9 + He-4 -> C-12 + n-1.

32.reason: The number of valence electrons determines the chemical properties of an element.

33.reason: The charge/mass (e/m) ratio of the electron is a universal constant — independent of the gas or electrode material in the discharge tube.

34.reason: X (Z=7,A=14) and Y (Z=7,A=15) are both nitrogen (config 2,5), so both have 5 valence electrons. (b) both have 2 shells; (c) config is 2,5 not 2,8,4; (d) X has 7n but Y has 8n.

35.reason: X2 has 34 electrons (=34 protons, neutral) and 40 neutrons per molecule. Per atom: Z = 17, neutrons = 20, mass = 37 -> 37/17 X.

36.reason: K+ and K- are both potassium: same protons (2) and same neutrons (3). Electrons differ (K+ has 18, K- has 20) and shells differ, so (a) and (d-statement) are false. Correct = (b) and (c).

37.reason: Rutherford's experiment showed that the mass and positive charge of an atom are concentrated in a tiny central nucleus.

41.reason: Energy shells increase in energy outward: K < L < M < N < O.

42.reason: 3 protons = lithium (Z=3), configuration 2,1 -> 1 valence electron -> valency 1.

43.reason: He2+ means a helium atom (Z=2) that has lost both its electrons -> 0 electrons remain.

44.reason: REVIEW: At small scattering angles the alpha-particle passes far from the nucleus through the electron cloud, so the nuclear charge is partly screened — Rutherford's formula assumes the whole nuclear charge is unscreened, which breaks down. NCERT-exemplar keyed answer is (a). (Option d on impact parameter is a plausible distractor; spot-check against the institute key.)

46.reason: X has Z=9 (9 protons), mass 19 -> 10 neutrons. X- has gained one electron -> 9+1 = 10 electrons. So E=10, P=9, N=10.

47.reason: The electron is the universal fundamental particle — present in every atom of every element.

48.reason: Atomic number equals the number of protons in the nucleus.

49.reason: Mole ratio C:H:N = 9/12 : 1/1 : 3.5/14 = 0.75:1:0.25 = 3:4:1. Empirical formula C3H4N (mass 54). Molecular mass 108 = 2 x 54 -> C6H8N2.

50.reason: O-16 has 16-8 = 8 neutrons. The carbon isotope with 8 neutrons is C-14 (6 protons + 8 neutrons), used in radiocarbon dating.

51.reason: Number of electrons = 30 kg / (9.1 x 10^-31 kg) = 3.3 x 10^31.

52.reason: REVIEW: Protons in Mg = 12 (Z=12). Neutrons in Mg-25 = 25-12 = 13. Average mass = (24x78.99 + 25x10 + 26x11.01)/100 = 24.32. Options (a) and (b) are printed identically (source duplicate); chose (a).

53.reason: REVIEW: Neutrons — Cd-114=66, Sn-119=69 (diff); Co-59=32, Ni-59=31 (diff); Cu-63=34, Cu-65=36 (diff). Statement iii: printed Cs-113 (58n) vs Xe-132 (78n) does NOT match, but Cs's natural isotope is Cs-133 (78n) which matches Xe-132 (78n) — the printed 113 is a clear source misprint for 133, making iii the only correct pair. Answer 'iii only' per the intended (corrected) figure; spot-check the source mass number.

54.reason: All hydrogen isotopes (protium, deuterium, tritium) have exactly 1 proton and 1 electron; equal positive and negative charge makes them electrically neutral.

55.reason: In a neutral atom the number of electrons equals the number of protons.

56.reason: Full shells: K=2, L=8, M=18, N=32 -> total = 2+8+18+32 = 60 electrons.

57.reason: Just as atomic number = number of protons, mass number = number of protons + number of neutrons.

58.reason: Valency 1 occurs in both metals (e.g. sodium, Na) and non-metals (e.g. chlorine, Cl).

59.reason: Isotopes of an element have the same Z but a different number of neutrons (hence different mass number).

60.reason: 1: carbon has 4 valence electrons, not 6 -> false. 2: 40/18 X and 40/20 Y have the same mass but different Z -> isobars, not isotopes -> false. 3: outermost-shell electrons determine valency -> true. 4: C-14, N-15, O-16 each have 8 neutrons -> isotones -> true. Correct = iii and iv.

39.reason: Q's outermost is the M shell (3rd) with 7 electrons = config 2,8,7 = Z 17 (chlorine), eliminating option a. P's outermost is the N shell (4th), so Z must be >= 19; among the options only 24 (chromium, 2,8,13,1) actually has an occupied N shell. So P = 24, Q = 17.

40.reason: A cation has fewer electrons than protons. All four diagrams show 10 electrons (shells 2,8). I: 10p,10e = neutral (Ne). II: 9p,10e = anion (F-). III: 12p,10e = +2 cation (Mg2+). IV: 13p,10e = +3 cation (Al3+). So III and IV are cations.
